title: Applied Project & Graduation
text: Vibe coding practice: build a website, portfolio or expense tracker
Testimonials, survey forms and programme feedback
Programme Q&A, next steps and close
notes: Day 5 is the applied project: a full morning of vibe coding, where each trainee builds a website, portfolio or expense tracker, then a showcase, feedback forms and testimonials. The afternoon is the graduation ceremony, photographs and a closing Q&A on next steps.

title: What Is Vibe Coding?
text: You are the boss. The AI is the builder.
notes:
Vibe coding has four steps. You describe the web page you want. The AI writes the code. You open it and test it. Then you ask for improvements.
You do not need to learn the code. You are the boss. The AI is the builder.
EXAMPLE: Like telling a builder 'I want a house with two bedrooms and a blue door.' You do not lay the bricks yourself.

title: The CLEAR Recipe
notes:
To build with AI, use the CLEAR recipe. Five letters.
C = Context: what is it, and who is it for? L = Language: say 'HTML in one single file'. E = Elements: the parts of the page. A = Appearance: colours and style. R = Result: what it should do, for example look good on a phone.
INTERPRETER: CLEAR is an English word that helps people remember. Explain each part; keep the letters in English.

title: 3 Projects Today
text: A page about you and your
An app that adds up your
Each project: a new chat and a new file.
notes:
Today you will build three real projects with AI, one after another.
Project 1: a portfolio, a web page about you and your skills.
Project 2: an expense tracker, an app that adds up your money.
Project 3: a photo album, a gallery for your photos.
These pictures are real pages, made with the same prompts you will use. Yours will look different, because you choose the words and colours.
RULE: Start a NEW chat and a NEW file for each project.

title: Copy, Save, Open
notes:
Four steps for every project.
1. Copy the code: click the Copy button under the code.
2. Open Notepad and paste.
3. Save it with a name that ends in .html: portfolio.html, then expenses.html, then album.html. In 'Save as type', choose 'All Files'.
4. Double-click the file. It opens in your browser. That is your website!
INTERPRETER: Show the steps on the projector while translating.

title: Project 1: Your Portfolio
text: Like a business card on the internet.
notes:
Project 1 is a portfolio: a web page that shows who you are, what you can do, and how to contact you.
It is like a business card on the internet. It works 24 hours a day.
Look at the example. It has five parts: a header with a menu, About me, Skills, Projects and Contact.
IDEA: If you have a small business (tailoring, hair, food, phone repair), you can make the page about your business instead.
SAFETY: Only a public email address. No phone number, no home address, no ID numbers.
Note: the example is a real page made for this course; 'Amina' is an invented name.

4. Projects: 3 cards with a title, short text and a View button

notes:
Fill in the [brackets] on paper first. Then type the prompt into Claude.
Check it with CLEAR: C, a portfolio for you. L, one HTML file. E, the five parts. A, your colours. R, good on a phone.
SMALL BUSINESS: change 'my name' to the business name, and 'skills' to services with prices.
SAFETY: public email only.
INTERPRETER: The prompt can be typed in English or in the participant's language.

title: Make It Better: Speak Normally
text: “The button does nothing. Make it open
notes:
Now improve your page. Talk to the AI in normal words. You do not need technical words.
Ask for one change at a time. After each change, copy, save and open again to test it.
EXAMPLES: 'Make the title bigger.' 'Change the background to light green.' 'Add a section with photos.' 'The button does nothing. Make it open WhatsApp.'

title: Project 2: The Expense Tracker
text: Like a money notebook that adds up by itself.
notes:
Project 2 is your first app that DOES things, not only shows things.
Many families keep a small book of money in and money out. This is the same book on a computer, but it adds up by itself.
Look at the example. You type a name and an amount, choose a type (Food, Transport, Bills), and press Add. The total updates by itself. The round chart shows where the money goes.
How could this help you or your family?
Note: the example is a real page made for this course.

title: Build It: The Expense Tracker
text: Build an expense tracker app in one HTML file, with the
A form: expense name, amount, and a type: Food,
When I click Add, show the expense in a list with a red
Show the total at the bottom. Update it by itself.
Show money in [YOUR CURRENCY]. Use [2 COLOURS].
notes:
Start a NEW chat for this project. Save the code as expenses.html.
Fill in your currency and colours, then send the prompt.
TEST: Add 3 expenses. Is the total right? Check with a calculator. Delete one: does the total go down? Press Add with an empty form: what happens? Refresh the page: where did your expenses go? (They disappear. The next slide fixes that.)

title: Make the Tracker Smarter
text: still there when I open the
notes:
Now add three more features. Send ONE prompt, test it, then send the next.
PROMPT 2, filter: shows only one type of spending, and its total.
PROMPT 3, save: the expenses stay after you close the page. They are saved only on this computer's browser.
PROMPT 4, chart: a round chart that shows where the money goes.
TIP: If something breaks, say what you see and ask the AI to fix only that part.

title: Project 3: The Photo Album
text: Like a family photo album, on your computer.
notes:
Project 3 is a photo album: like the family albums people pass around, but on the computer.
Look at the example: a neat grid of photos, a caption under each one, album names (Family, Friends, Travel), a search box and an Upload button. Click a photo to see it big.
PRIVACY: Only use photos you are allowed to use. Ask people before you put their photo in, and do not put photos of other people's children online.
Note: the example is a real page made for this course, with free photos from Unsplash.

title: Build It: The Photo Album
text: After Prompt 2: click a photo to see it
Create a photo album web app in one HTML file. Show photos in a
grid of 3 columns, with a caption and an album name (Family, Friends
or Travel) under each photo. Use sample photos from picsum.photos
for now. On a phone, show 1 column.
PROMPT 2 · CLICK TO SEE IT BIG
When I click a photo, show it big in the middle of a dark screen, with
the caption below. An × button closes it. The Escape key also closes
Next: ask for an Upload button and a Search box.
notes:
New chat, new file: album.html. Send Prompt 1, test it, then send Prompt 2.
Prompt 1 makes the grid with sample photos. Prompt 2 adds the 'lightbox': click a photo and it opens big on a dark screen, like the picture on the right.
MORE (if there is time): 'Add an Upload button so I can add my own photos.' 'Add a search box that shows only photos whose caption has my words.'
NOTE: Uploaded photos may disappear when you refresh. That is normal for practice.

title: When Something Goes Wrong
text: Tell the AI what you see.
notes:
Problems are normal. Here is what to do.
Blank or broken page? Tell the AI what you see: 'The page is blank. What went wrong?'
Not what you wanted? Describe it again, with more detail.
The same error again and again? Start a new chat. Paste your last code that worked, and describe the problem.
Ask yourself: what information was missing from my prompt?

title: Build Your 3 Projects
notes:
PRACTICAL 7 · ABOUT 75 MINUTES · ON YOUR OWN
Build the three projects, one after another. Start a new chat and a new file for each one.
Portfolio: about 20 minutes. Expense tracker: about 25 minutes. Photo album: about 25 minutes.
For each: fill in the prompt, send it, copy-save-open, then make at least one improvement.
TRAINER: Walk around and help. When someone is stuck, ask: 'What did you tell the AI? What is missing?' Fast learners can do the extra prompts (filter, save, chart, upload, search).
SAFETY: public email only; no home address; only photos you are allowed to use.

title: Show and Tell
notes:
Swap seats with a partner. Look at their page.
Two stars: tell them two things you like. One wish: suggest one change, and the prompt they could use to make it.
Then two or three people show their page on the projector.
To share your page online for free, ask the trainer after the session.

title: REMEMBER
text: A clear prompt gets a better answer
Use the 4 parts: task, background, information, style
Build in small steps: describe, test, improve
notes:
Thank you for your hard work today. You learned what AI is, how to talk to it, and you built your own web page.
Keep practising, a little every day. Take questions.
INTERPRETER: Thank you for your help today.
